d.d: An administrative division of the later Roman Empire, established by the Herodian tetrarchy.
An ecclesiastical territory administered by a bishop.
Of or relating to the Roman emperor Diocletian.
An electronic device that allows current to flow in one direction only; used chiefly as a rectifier.
any organic compound having two hydroxy functional groups
A three-dimensional display of a scenery, often having a painted background in front of which models are arranged, e.g. in a museum where stuffed animals are presented against a painted landscape.
Abbreviation of distal intestinal obstruction syndrome.
Any oxide containing two oxygen atoms in each molecule.
The unsaturated six-membered heterocycle having four carbon atoms, two oxygen atoms, and two double bonds (molecular formula C₄H₄O₂); 1,2-dioxin and 1,4-dioxin.
The parent compound dibenzo-1,4-dioxin or dibenzo-p-dioxin (molecular formula C₁₂H₈O₂), in which two benzene rings are connected through two oxygen atoms; dibenzodioxin, oxanthrene.
Any of a broad range of toxic or carcinogenic halogenated polycyclic compounds that occur as byproducts of herbicides.
